bull_bear.body:
- **Sharp deleveraging:** gross DER 0.18 (FY25 0.39); **net DER 0.09**; net borrowings ₹973 cr.
- Highest-ever dividend **₹62/share** (interim ₹8 + final ₹54), first-ever interim — strong shareholder-reward stance balanced with growth capex.
- Stated discipline: optimum return on value-added/growth projects, capital discipline maintained.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation / deleveraging

bull_bear.body:
- **GRM volatility / export-duty & RTP cap:** Export duty imposed 26-March FY26; cracks volatile daily; netback after duty adjustment could turn negative short-term (investors pressed hard). Mgmt deflects to monthly averages "near long-term."
- **Single-site concentration:** entire business is one Manali refinery (3 crude units) — H2 FY27 Sep–Oct M&I will dent throughput.
- **Geopolitical crude sourcing:** Strait of Hormuz closure (>50 days referenced); 30–40% of Middle East term supply disrupted over a short window (back-filled via spot); reliant on suppliers honoring annual commitments.
- **Forex:** rupee depreciation drove ~₹350–400 cr FY26 loss (other expenses).
- **CBR execution/funding:** not addressed — overhang of large new refinery JV remains uncommented.
- Customer concentration: ~90% offtake to IOC at RTP (limited pricing autonomy).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident, operationally proud (repeated "highest ever," "stellar," "best"). Deliberately refuses to give short-term/daily numbers ("I'm not a trader"; focus on long-term averages and business model integrity). Transparent on GRM split (core vs reported) and forex when pressed; deflects on RTP/OMC discount mechanics and CBR. Strong emphasis on capital discipline + shareholder reward.
bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Core vs reported GRM gap of ~$3.45/bbl in Q4 = inventory gain** — Q4 headline $13.75 flattered by inventory; core $10.3 is the cleaner number.
- Niche products are only 7–8% of volume but **~15% of margins** — outsized margin lever.
- DCU utilization jump (70% → ~100%) is a structural yield improvement, not cyclical.
- Mgmt explicitly de-links crude price level from GRM (crack-driven) — counters the investor narrative that high crude = low GRM.
- "Other expenses" surge (Q4 ₹634 cr vs ₹344 cr) is mostly forex, not opex inflation — a presentation/disclosure issue mgmt acknowledged.
- Bonus issue is on the table given tiny ₹148 cr share capital vs ₹11,000 cr reserves.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious points

bull_bear.body:
- Captive route to market through the parent: approximately 92% of production is marketed through IndianOil's extensive marketing network, the remaining 8% directly marketed by CPCL
- Crude/feedstock flexibility: in FY 2025-26 CPCL trial-processed and commercialized six new crude grades - WTI Midland (USA), Qatar Marine (Qatar), Nile Blend (Sudan), Sarir/Messla Blend (Libya), Sankofa (Ghana) and Rabi Blend (Gabon) - and handled nine VLCC cargoes
- Energy efficiency benchmark: first Indian PSU refinery to achieve a Quartile-1 ranking in the Solomon Energy Intensity Index global benchmarking
- Best-ever physical performance in FY 2025-26: highest-ever crude throughput 11.71 MMT, best-ever distillate yield 79.1%, lowest-ever Energy Intensity Index (EII) of 84.0, best-ever MBN of 69.8 and historic-low Fuel & Loss of 7.73%
- Elevated as the 28th Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise by the Department of Public Enterprises, Government of India, in June 2026, carrying enhanced operating autonomy
- Strategic location, established logistics and marketing linkages, diversified crude processing capability and access to growing domestic fuel markets [back-filled from the risks_esg bundle, 'Sustaining Competitive Strength']
- In-house R&D with the CPCL-IIT Madras Research Cell and industry-academia collaborations; three patents filed during the year
- Water resilience: refinery continues to operate with zero fresh water consumption for refining operations, supported by its own desalination and treated-water infrastructure
- Ranked second amongst Indian oil and gas companies with an S&P Global ESG Score of 60 for 2025; awarded the ICAI Gold Shield for Excellence in Financial Reporting
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Market volatility in crude and product prices / refining margin volatility — BRSR material issue #3 (Risk): 'Fluctuations in international crude oil prices, refining margins and demand-supply dynamics directly influence profitability, cash flows and business performance', with negative implications of margin compression, earnings volatility and inventory valuation impacts. Named first among key risks in the ERM framework. Mitigation: diversify crude sourcing, optimise refinery configuration, integrated margin management, inventory optimisation and market intelligence.
- Crude supply disruption and import dependence — Crude supply disruptions are a named key risk under the enterprise risk framework; the FY 2026-27 outlook flags 'potential supply disruptions from key crude-producing regions', and for India 'crude oil import dependence is expected to remain significant, necessitating continued emphasis on supply diversification, strategic reserves, and refinery flexibility'.
- Government policy and fiscal intervention / regulatory compliance — The FY 2026-27 outlook explicitly names 'Government policy interventions, including Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED) and other fiscal measures' as a factor influencing refining margins. BRSR material issue #7 (Risk) adds that 'the refining and petroleum sector operates in a highly regulated environment with evolving environmental, safety and operational requirements', with penalties, legal liabilities, operational restrictions and reputational impact on non-compliance.
- Energy transition and climate change (physical and transition risk) — BRSR material issue #1 (Risk & Opportunity): climate change presents physical and transition risks through extreme weather, evolving regulations, carbon pricing and changing stakeholder expectations; negative implications are increased compliance costs, carbon pricing exposure and operational disruptions. Energy transition developments are also a named ERM key risk.
- Water availability, water and wastewater management — BRSR material issue #10 (Risk & Opportunity): water is a critical operational resource and effective wastewater treatment is essential for regulatory compliance and long-term resource security; negative implications are increased operating costs and regulatory risks. Water security is separately named as a risk the Company monitors proactively. (The supplied text is truncated mid-sentence in this row.)
- Asset integrity, process safety and occupational health & safety — BRSR material issues #8 and #9 (both Risk): refinery operations involve hazardous processes where employee and contractor safety is critical, and safe operation of critical assets is essential to prevent process safety incidents, unplanned shutdowns and environmental impacts; negative implications include workplace incidents, production losses, business interruptions, repair costs, regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
- Cybersecurity — Cybersecurity threats are a named key risk in the enterprise-wide risk management framework and among the emerging risks the Company is strengthening its framework against, alongside energy transition, climate change, water availability and evolving environmental regulations; the Company maintains proactive oversight over cybersecurity.
- Project execution risk — Project execution challenges are explicitly listed among the key risks subject to continuous review and mitigation through structured governance mechanisms - material given the Rs 1,620 Crore / 256 TMTPA LOBS project at Manali, the CBRPL construction exposure and the phased retail-outlet rollout.
- Customer and related-party concentration (structural, not labelled as a risk) — CPCL markets approximately 92% of its production through IndianOil's network and 'primarily concentrates on supplying its petroleum products to its parent company, IOCL'; BRSR reports sales to related parties at 93.92% of total sales (FY 2024-25: 94.71%) and investments in related parties at 99.08% of total investments. Geographic concentration is equally structural: operations in 1 State, 'Nil' international markets, exports only as a supporting manufacturer through IOCL (9.67% share). [Concentration percentages back-filled from the capex_expansion bundle's BRSR 'Open-ness of business' block.]
- Governance / Board composition non-compliance — As on 31.03.2026 the Company had one Independent Director against a stated requirement of 10, and no Woman Independent Director against the minimum requirement of one, because the power to appoint directors vests with the Government of India; BRSR also reports 0% female representation on the Board and among KMP. BRSR material issue #5 flags regulatory action, financial penalties and reputational risks arising from governance failures. [Board-composition shortfall back-filled from the governance_entities bundle's Corporate Governance Report.]

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries

business.body: CPCL's single main activity is manufacturing - 'Processing of Crude Oil into Refined Petroleum products and other products' - accounting for 100% of turnover per BRSR Section A. Its diversified product portfolio comprises transportation fuels, petrochemicals, industrial products and specialty products; approximately 92% of production is marketed through IndianOil's extensive marketing network and the remaining 8% is directly marketed by CPCL. It supplies primarily its parent IOCL, sells feedstock to nearby petrochemical industries, directly markets specialty items and by-products (Food Grade Hexane, Mineral Turpentine Oil, Paraffin Wax, Sulphur, Petroleum Coke) to end consumers, and during FY 2025-26 entered fuel retailing under its own CPCL SOOPER brand.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Transportation fuels:** High Speed Diesel (HSD), Motor Spirit (MS), Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF), LPG, Kerosene
- **Industrial and bulk products:** Naphtha, Bitumen / Asphalt, Fuel Oil, Petroleum Coke (Petcoke), Sulphur
- **Petrochemicals and feedstocks:** Propylene, Butene-2, LABFS, MEKFS, PBFS
- **Specialty products:** Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS), Food Grade Hexane, pharma grade Hexane, Mineral Turpentine Oil (MTO), Paraffin Wax, Pentane (production trials completed in the Propane Recovery Unit), specialty solvents
- **Retail fuel:** CPCL SOOPER branded retail outlets

Classification is inconsistent within the AR - BRSR Section A item 23 lists it as a 'Joint Venture' while Form AOC-1 Part B describes significant influence as 'Associate'. IndianOil's Board on 28.03.2024 accorded in-principle approval to revise CBRPL's capital structure to 75% IndianOil / 25% CPCL; the existing structure (CPCL 25%, IOCL 25%, other seed investors 50%) continues pending CCEA approvals, after which CBRPL would become a subsidiary of IndianOil. CPCL also holds share warrants in CBRPL

latest_quarter.body:
- **FY26 GRM $9.28/bbl vs Singapore $5.83** (premium ~$3.45); **Q4 GRM $13.75 vs Singapore $8.70**. Premium sustained 5–6 years via crude optimization, product distribution, procurement efficiency.
- **Core Q4 GRM ~$10.3/bbl** (inventory-adjusted).
- No 1:1 link between crude price and GRM — it's the crack (product minus crude) that drives GRM; mgmt won't quantify "profit foregone" on RTP since it sells at industry transfer price.
- **Crude geography (normalized mix):** India ~10% (incl. Bombay High), **Russia ~25–30%**, rest mostly Middle East (incl. Iraq), ~5–10% Africa & US. Russian taken only when cheapest on landed-cost basis.
- **Crude sourcing:** 55–60% via 1-year term contracts (almost all Middle East, at OSP), rest spot. Term volumes "intact," 1–2 cargoes flex.
- Crude inventory ~5–18 days (target ~20 days normal, run lean given disruption); product inventory minimal (few days, IOC offtake adjacent).

New capex: Group 2/3 LOBS ₹1,600 cr (250 KTPA), retail ₹400 cr, debottlenecking study (EIL) ongoing. Forex loss Q4 ~₹200 cr / FY ~₹350–400 cr. GRM guided near long-term avg ~$13/bbl post export-duty. outlook.body:
- **GRM outlook:** Mgmt repeatedly states current net GRM/cracks (diesel + ATF) are **"close to long-term average ~$13/bbl"** even after the 26-March export duty imposition. They monitor on a monthly/fortnightly basis, not daily. Implication: despite RTP cap / export-duty noise, margins are holding near long-run levels.
- **Throughput:** First-half FY27 — **no M&I (maintenance & inspection) planned → expect sustained ~110–111% util**. A **scheduled M&I of one refinery unit around Sep–Oct 2026** will affect H2 throughput.
- **Cauvery Basin Refinery (CBR):** **NOT discussed on this call.** No progress / funding / capex commentary provided by management.
- **Capex (FY27 and beyond):**
  - Group 2/3 LOBS project: **₹1,600 cr**
  - Retail outlets (~300 licenses): **₹400 cr**
  - → New projects total **₹2,000 cr, spread over 2–3 years**
  - Plus **~₹500 cr/yr normal maintenance capex**
  - Potential ADDITIONAL low-cost debottlenecking capex (study ongoing with EIL, not yet frozen/in plan)
  - FY26 actual capex: **₹856 cr** (vs ₹673 cr FY25)
- **Debt:** Guidance is comfort — net DER ~0.1, ample headroom to borrow for profitable schemes.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- FY26 crude throughput **11.71 MMT = 112% of 10.5 MMTPA installed** (record); Q4 **2.93 MMT = 111%**.
- Consistently exceeding 10.5 MMTPA for last 3–4 years (11.6–11.7 MMT range). Capacity rated on ~330 standard operating days; high upkeep + low unplanned interruptions create leeway above nameplate.
- Fuel & loss best-ever **7.73%**; MBN best **69.8%**; EII best **84%**. Distillate yield record **79.1%** (prior best 77.6% in FY20). DCU (Delayed Coker) now running near **100%** vs ~70% earlier — key yield driver.
- Record production: HSD **5.139 MMT**, MS **1.318 MMT**, LPG **447 TMT** (vs prior best 404 in FY24).
- Crude slate FY26: **52% high-sulphur / 48% low-sulphur** (refinery can run up to 70% HS; chose more LS as it was cheaper → higher yield, lower fuel & loss).
outlook.title: Throughput / pipeline detail

outlook.body:
- **Group 2/3 LOBS project (₹1,600 cr):** CPCL is the **only Indian refinery with liquid fuels + wax + lube potential**; currently produces only Group 1 LOBS. New unit adds **250 KTPA Group 2/3 capacity** (currently imported in India) → import substitution + value addition; **IRR-driven (not compliance)**; some HSD converts to higher-realization LOBS.
- **Fuel retail (₹400 cr):** ~300 retail outlet licenses taken; commissioning to ramp in FY27 — extends value chain refining → refining + marketing.
- **Low-cost debottlenecking:** EIL study (incomplete; expected to finish FY27) to add secondary capacity matching the demonstrated higher primary throughput → sustain higher margins. Not yet in capex plan.
- **Niche product ramp:** Hexane capacity doubled (30 → 60); MTO more than doubled YoY; further ramp expected FY27.
- ~**RLNG consumption** for economics/sustainability.
- Investor floated **bonus issue** (share capital only ₹148 cr vs reserves ~₹11,000 cr) — mgmt said Board will consider "at the right time."
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the competitiveness of the core refining business through production of Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks, advanced process optimization and digital transformation
- Extend presence across the downstream value chain by entering retail fuel marketing (first Retail Outlet established 22nd March 2026; first COCO outlet commissioned at Mathur, Chennai on 20th May 2026), establishing a direct interface with customers
- Crude slate optimization and feedstock diversification - trial-processing and commercializing new crude grades and handling VLCC cargoes to reduce geographic dependence and optimize crude costs and refining margins
- Product diversification into specialty and high-value streams - pharma grade Hexane, specialty solvents, downstream petrochemical feedstocks, Pentane production trials in the Propane Recovery Unit, with commercial feasibility completed for Pentane/Heptane-rich streams, VLSFO, De-aromatized Kerosene, specialty drilling fluids and industrial solvent grades
- Innovation and IP: continuous investment in research, process improvements, digital technologies and advanced analytics; strengthened IP portfolio through industry-academia collaborations with three patents filed during the year
- Sustainability embedded in strategy: advance renewable energy deployment, energy efficiency, water optimisation, circular economy practices and GHG reduction toward Net Zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 by 2046
- Digital transformation of governance and operations - in-house Tender Management System integrated with SAP and GeM, FASTag-enabled automated weighbridges, CPCL Retail Outlet Portal, upgraded Oil Management and Storage DCS, Virtual Reality-based Training Laboratory
- People and leadership pipeline: GUIDE Framework launched to institutionalize mentoring, leadership development and knowledge transfer, plus targeted leadership interventions
- Leverage enhanced autonomy from Navratna CPSE status (28th Navratna, conferred June 2026) to accelerate strategic initiatives and pursue growth opportunities with greater agility
- Positioning for the energy transition by leveraging refining expertise, investing in cleaner technologies, expanding downstream presence, strengthening digital capabilities and enhancing organizational resilience
- CPCL maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy and a Policy on Related Party Transactions among the governance policies posted on its website, so payout is governed by a stated policy framework rather than ad-hoc decision; as a Government Company under MoP&NG administrative control, capital and appointment decisions ultimately sit with the Government of India. For FY 2025-26 the 60th AGM notice puts to members a Final Equity dividend of Rs 54 per Equity Share, and a Preference dividend of 6.65% (Rs 0.665 per Preference Share) on the outstanding Preference Shares up to their redemption date of September 23, 2025 - the preference shares having been redeemed during the year. Together with the maiden interim dividend of Rs 8 per share this makes a highest-ever total of Rs 62 per share for the year, alongside management's stated intent of prudent capital deployment, disciplined cost management and consistent shareholder returns [dividend-total and philosophy sentences back-filled from the Chairman/Board message in the profile and strategy_outlook bundles]. Balance-sheet and leverage figures are deliberately not reproduced here.
- Net Zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2046 - the Company's stated decarbonisation roadmap, reinforced through renewable energy deployment
- FY 2025-26 emissions disclosed as Scope 1 of 2.58 million metric tonnes of CO2 equivalent and Scope 2 of 53,432 metric tonnes of CO2 equivalent, with Scope 1+2 intensity reducing to 0.22 tCO2e/MT of crude throughput. The Scope 3 figure is printed as '32.53 metric tonnes of CO2 equivalent', which is implausible for a refinery and is reproduced here verbatim without correction. [Back-filled from the capex_expansion bundle's Natural Capital block.]
- Renewable portfolio of 17.6 MW wind (Pushpathur Wind Farm) and 3.4 MW solar, stated as 21 MW total renewable energy; a floating solar plant (1.1 MW per the narrative, 1.14 MW per BRSR) was commissioned in October 2025
- Renewable energy consumption increased to 123.82 BTJ in FY 2025-26, a 32.4% increase over FY 2024-25, supported by expanded generation, higher renewable power procurement and greater use of cleaner fuels such as RLNG
- Lowest-ever Energy Intensity Index (EII) of 84.0 and 21 energy conservation projects implemented; first Indian PSU refinery to achieve a Quartile-1 ranking in the Solomon Energy Intensity Index global benchmarking
- Water stewardship: over 6% reduction in water footprint while continuing to operate with zero fresh water consumption for refining operations; expanded water recycling and reuse, strengthened ETP and DMRO systems, indigenous desalination membrane technology, and an additional 44,100 m3 of storm water storage
- Circular-economy R&D: patented green corrosion inhibitor made from oil waste for E20 fuel applications, nanocellulose produced from rice straw (reducing stubble burning), and a green hydrogen production process using RO reject water - 100% of R&D and capex investments stated to be in technologies improving environmental and social impacts
- BRSR for FY 2025-26 prepared on a standalone basis (excluding JV and associates) with Reasonable Assurance from Bureau Veritas (India) Private Limited
- Ranked second amongst Indian oil and gas companies with an S&P Global ESG Score of 60 for 2025; awarded the ICAI Gold Shield for Excellence in Financial Reporting
- Zero tolerance record on conduct: 'Nil' monetary penalties/fines, settlements and compounding fees and 'Nil' non-monetary imprisonment/punishment in the reporting year; zero disciplinary actions against Directors/KMPs/employees/workers for bribery or corruption in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25; zero conflict-of-interest complaints against Directors or KMPs
- Grievance redressal disclosed by stakeholder group for FY 2025-26 with all complaints resolved: Communities 20 filed / 0 pending, Investors and Shareholders 17 filed / 0 pending, Employees and workers 5 filed / Nil pending, Customers 1 filed (Petcoke quality - powdery instead of granular, addressed by adjusting plant process parameters), Environment NIL, Public Policy 0
- Workforce and diversity: 1,403 employees as on 31 March 2026 including 87 women (739 Executives, 664 Non-Executives); permanent employees 10% female and permanent workers 2% female; 20 differently abled employees and 18 differently abled workers; 0% female representation on the Board of Directors and among Key Management Personnel; employee turnover 3.42% and worker turnover 1.85% in FY 2025-26 (improving from 4.39% and 2.19%)
- Safety embedded through rigorous training, emergency preparedness, Behaviour-Based Safety (BBS) initiatives and continuous improvement in operational practices; industrial relations stated as stable and cordial throughout the year
- Value-chain engagement: 11 awareness programmes for value chain partners covering GeM procurement, MSE and MII preference, category-wise materials/services and participation of MSE women entrepreneurs, covering 100% of value chain partners by value of business [back-filled from the capex_expansion bundle's BRSR Leadership Indicators]

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: CPCL's headline growth project is the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) Project at the Manali Refinery, stated at a cost of Rs 1,620 Crore with a capacity of 256 TMTPA, expected to enhance product diversification, strengthen value addition and expand presence in the high-value lubricant base oil segment; the BRSR adds that the LOBS project 'will support import substitution' (that sentence is cut off mid-clause in the supplied text). No commissioning or completion date is stated for LOBS anywhere in the routed text. The refinery operates against a nameplate capacity of 10.5 MMTPA and delivered a best-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMTPA in FY 2025-26 with a record distillate yield of 79.1% - throughput and yield are performance, not capacity, and no crude-capacity expansion is announced. Sustainability-linked capex completed during the year: a floating solar power plant (stated as 1.1 MW commissioned in October 2025 in the Chairman/ESG narrative and as 1.14 MW in BRSR Principle 2 - the AR is internally inconsistent on this figure), taking total installed solar to 3.4 MW alongside 17.6 MW of wind at the Pushpathur Wind Farm for a stated total renewable capacity of 21 MW; storm water management infrastructure expanded with an additional storage capacity of 44,100 m3; improved marine logistics; 21 energy conservation projects implemented; and under the Desalination Product Water Pipeline Project GRP pipelines were delivered on 17.11.2025. Ongoing projects named in BRSR Principle 2 are high-efficiency furnace replacement, condensate recovery revamp, 400 kV grid upgradation and desalination pipeline augmentation, expected to reduce energy consumption, GHG emissions and water footprint. Forward intent stated in the Natural Capital section: planning to upgrade grid import infrastructure to facilitate higher renewable power integration, and exploring renewable energy development through Joint Ventures, Renewable Power Purchase Agreements and other implementation models. Downstream expansion: first Retail Outlet established 22nd March 2026 and first Company-Owned Company-Operated (COCO) outlet commissioned at Mathur, Chennai on 20th May 2026 under the CPCL SOOPER brand, with phased development of further retail outlets. Associate-level capital exposure: the capital commitment in respect of Cauvery Basin Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (CBRPL, units under construction) stands at Rs 2,272.01 Cr as at March 31, 2026, disclosed separately from other capital commitments. R&D and capex investments in technologies improving environmental and social impacts are stated at 100% of total R&D and capex investments in both the current and previous financial year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India is expected to become the largest contributor to global oil demand growth between 2023 and 2030, accounting for more than one-third of global oil demand growth during the period
- IEA projects global oil demand to reach around 104.5 MBPD in 2026 (from about 103.8 MBPD in 2025), with non-OECD Asia remaining the principal source of incremental demand and petrochemical feedstocks accounting for an increasing share of future demand growth
- The outlook for FY 2026-27 remains uncertain: the IEA expects oil markets to remain broadly well supplied, while geopolitical tensions, OPEC+ policy decisions, trade developments and supply chain disruptions remain key drivers of crude oil prices
- The refining sector is likely to face continued volatility in crude prices, product margins, freight rates and trade flows, necessitating agile crude sourcing and operational strategies
- Product crack spreads improved materially in FY 2025-26, supported by tighter global balances, supply disruptions and strong transport fuel demand, with elevated diesel cracks driving refining margins
- Ability to process a diverse range of crude grades enhances operational flexibility and supports margin optimization; expanded crude basket has enhanced supply security and reduced dependence on specific geographies
- India remains one of the world's largest crude oil importers, with imported crude accounting for over 85% of domestic crude oil requirements, so the composition of the crude import basket is critical to refinery economics
- RBI projects Indian real GDP growth at 6.9% for 2026-27; elevated energy and commodity prices together with disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz are expected to weigh on growth during the year
- Global energy demand growth moderated to approximately 1.3% in 2025 from 2.0% in 2024; Brent averaged around US$70-75 per barrel during much of 2025 before approaching US$90-100 per barrel amid Middle East tensions late in FY 2025-26
- For FY 2026-27 the domestic refining industry faces a mixed outlook - refining margins may be influenced by crude/product price volatility, potential supply disruptions from key crude-producing regions, government policy interventions including Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED), fluctuations in petrochemical feedstock prices and demand, and exchange-rate and freight-cost movements [back-filled from the risks_esg bundle, MD&A 'Outlook for FY 2026-27']
- Management states CPCL will continue to focus on operational excellence, crude basket diversification, feedstock flexibility, energy efficiency, digital transformation and disciplined cost management to enhance resilience and sustain profitability [back-filled from the risks_esg bundle]
- Ongoing investments in refinery modernization, energy efficiency, digitalization and sustainability initiatives are expected to strengthen resilience and support long-term growth [back-filled from the risks_esg bundle]

deepdive.thesis: Single-site Manali refinery (IOC subsidiary) delivering record throughput (112% util) and premium GRMs ($9.2/bbl FY26 vs $5.83 Singapore), now sharply de-levered (net DER 0.09) and pivoting capex into higher-value Group 2/3 lube base oils + fuel retail, while navigating heavy geopolitical crude-sourcing disruption.

open.item: CPCL commits to achieve Net Zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2046.

CPCL is implementing the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) Project at the Manali Refinery at a cost of Rs 1,620 Crore with a capacity of 256 TMTPA, to expand into the high-value lubricant base oil segment and support import substitution.

CPCL is entering fuel retail marketing under its own brand, having established its first Retail Outlet on 22nd March 2026 and commissioned its first Company-Owned Company-Operated (COCO) outlet at Mathur, Chennai on 20th May 2026, extending its presence across the downstream value chain.
The Desalination Product Water Pipeline Project is progressing, with GRP pipelines delivered on 17.11.2025.

CPCL completed commercial feasibility assessments for several high-value products - Pentane-rich streams, Heptane-rich streams, Very Low Sulphur Fuel Oil (VLSFO), De-aromatized Kerosene, specialty drilling fluids and industrial solvent grades - as new revenue streams.
CPCL is expanding into retail fuel marketing, having established its first Retail Outlet on 22nd March 2026 and commissioned its first COCO retail outlet at Mathur, Chennai on 20th May 2026.
CPCL is pursuing production of Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks as a core-refining competitiveness initiative alongside advanced process optimization and digital transformation.

Ongoing projects - high-efficiency furnace replacement, condensate recovery revamp, 400 kV grid upgradation and desalination pipeline augmentation - are expected to reduce energy consumption, greenhouse gas emissions and water footprint and improve resource efficiency.
CPCL is planning to upgrade grid import infrastructure to facilitate higher renewable power integration and strengthen long-term energy resilience.

CPCL is exploring renewable energy development through Joint Ventures (JVs), Renewable Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) and other suitable implementation models to accelerate renewable energy adoption.

risks.note: BRSR material issue #3 (Risk): 'Fluctuations in international crude oil prices, refining margins and demand-supply dynamics directly influence profitability, cash flows and business performance', with negative implications of margin compression, earnings volatility and inventory valuation impacts. Named first among key risks in the ERM framework. Mitigation: diversify crude sourcing, optimise refinery configuration, integrated margin management, inventory optimisation and market intelligence.
